deploy.description: Notion Expense Claims automation webhook (Status -> Approved) -> resolve the claimant (Created by) to their Xero contact by email -> raise a DRAFT Xero bill EXP-<Claim ID> against that contact, account by Category, receipt attached -> write the bill link back to the claim's 'Xero bill' property.

trigger.trigger_note: Catch hook. A Notion database automation on Expense Claims ('When Status is set to Approved' -> Send webhook) POSTs the page here; `webhook_url` is the URL to paste into that automation. The workflow re-reads the page and bills only a claim whose Status is Approved, so a stray POST or a test ping does nothing. Re-setting Status to Approved re-fires it, which is the normal way to retry a claim after fixing it. Catch hooks drop a repeat POST whose top-level `id` was already seen (W6ZE93-VMEWP); Notion's automation payload has no top-level `id` (the page is under `data`), so repeat approvals of one claim are delivered.

notion.note: Write-back + guard property: 'Xero bill' (url), added 2026-10-07 with this Zap. Category options 'Training & courses', 'Events & sponsorship' and 'Memberships & publications' were added the same day. The data source is shared with the Zapier Notion integration (verified 2026-10-07). No page is created here, so repo rule 5 (default template) does not apply.
notion.automation: Configured by hand in Notion, not machine-verifiable: Expense Claims -> 'When Status is set to Approved' -> Send webhook to trigger.webhook_url.

xero.tax: SGD claims: line amounts tax-inclusive at the account's default tax rate (line_tax_type omitted). Any other currency: NoTax.
xero.contact_match: Notion user email (GET /v1/users/{created_by}) == Xero Contact.EmailAddress, active contacts only. No match or several matches fails the run; no contact is ever created.
